Description: Gates 2GT toothed idlers are used at the inner XY belt path reversal points in Voron CoreXY builds where the belt wraps with the tooth side inward. Outer belt reversals use smooth F695 bearings instead. Mismatching toothed and smooth idler positions causes belt noise and eventual skipping.
Verdict Label: OEM toothed idler — used where belt reversal requires tooth engagement
Cons: Only used at specific inner belt path reversal points — most idler positions use smooth F695 bearings
Name: 2GT Toothed Idler
Pros:
OEM tooth profile matched to Gates belt — zero pitch mismatch at tooth reversal points
Used at belt path reversal points where a smooth idler would cause belt tooth rotation and skip
Pre-assembled with integrated bearing

Description: Trianglelab’s 2GT 20T drive pulley is a reliable quality clone for most builds. At normal and moderate acceleration, it performs indistinguishably from Gates. For a performance build chasing every marginal improvement, Gates is still correct.
Verdict Label: Reliable quality clone pulley — works well in practice, sold by trusted ecosystem vendors
Cons:
Tooth profile is close to 2GT spec but not manufacturer-certified — slight mesh variation possible
For maximum performance builds, Gates pulley matched to Gates belt eliminates one variable
Name: Trianglelab 2GT 20T Drive Pulley
Pros:
Trianglelab has a track record of acceptable dimensional accuracy on motion components
Considerably cheaper than Gates — meaningful savings for AWD builds needing 4 pulleys
Sold through Trianglelab’s AliExpress store with some vendor accountability

Name: CNC All Wheel Drive Kit for Voron V2.4 and Trident

Description: The Gates 2GT 20T drive pulley is the XY motor pulley specified in Voron BOM and used in all prosumer CoreXY builds. OEM match for Gates LL-2GT belt. Bore is typically 5mm for standard NEMA17 motor shafts.
Verdict Label: OEM pulley for all Voron and CoreXY XY motor drives — machined to 2GT spec
Cons: Requires correct bore size for motor shaft diameter — double-check 5mm bore before ordering
Name: Gates 2GT 20T Drive Pulley
Pros:
Manufactured to match Gates LL-2GT belt precisely — tooth mesh geometry is designed as a matched set
20 tooth count is the Voron and CoreXY standard — all BOM and speed calculations assume 20T
Flanged to retain belt lateral position on the motor shaft

Name: Hybrid Ceramic Bearing Kit for Voron

Description: T8x8 300mm lead screws serve 250mm Voron 2.4 builds and all Voron Trident Z axes. Trident uses 3 lead screws for independent Z leveling (Quad Gantry Leveling equivalent). All other characteristics are the same as the 400mm variant.
Verdict Label: Z lead screw for 250mm Voron V2.4 and Voron Trident
Cons: Same lead screw limitations as 400mm variant — belted Z is the upgrade path for V2.4; Trident uses screws by design
Name: T8 Lead Screw 8mm Lead 300mm
Pros:
Correct length for 250mm V2.4 and Voron Trident (3 screws) — shorter span reduces lead screw whip at higher Z speeds
Same T8x8 spec as 400mm — all documentation and hardware is interchangeable except length

Description: Gates LL-2GT 6mm belt is the specified XY drive belt for Voron Design printers and is the de facto standard for all prosumer CoreXY self-builds. The 6mm width fits standard V2.4, Trident, 0.2, VzBot, and HevORT drive configurations. Gates is the OEM; all clone belts are measured against its dimensional accuracy and elasticity.
Verdict Label: The standard XY drive belt for all Voron and most prosumer CoreXY builds
Cons:
Requires cutting to length from bulk roll — sold per meter, not pre-sized
Slightly more expensive per meter than eSUN or generic alternatives
Name: Gates 2GT Belt 6mm
Pros:
Gates LL-2GT is the OEM belt specification for Voron, RatRig, and VzBot — it is what the pulleys and idlers are sized for
Polyurethane construction with fiberglass tension members — consistent stretch coefficient and lifetime under tension
No quality lottery — all Gates belt is manufactured to the same spec

Description: Generic 2GT 6mm belts from unknown manufacturers have no guaranteed tooth profile accuracy. Even minor pitch variation produces resonance artifacts that Input Shaper cannot correct. eSUN is only marginally more expensive and is a substantial quality improvement.
Verdict Label: Unknown manufacturer belt — tooth profile accuracy is untested and resonance behavior is unpredictable
Cons:
Tooth pitch accuracy is not guaranteed — pitch variation causes ghost ringing that Input Shaper cannot fully correct
Stretch characteristics are unknown — belt tension calibration becomes guesswork
eSUN is available at a small premium and is a meaningful quality step up
Name: Generic 2GT Belt 6mm
Pros: Lowest cost option — occasionally used by budget builders who accept the trade-offs

Name: XY Joint and Tensioner Kit for K3

Description: LDO is a Taiwanese linear motion manufacturer that produces MGN-profile rails to a quality level equivalent to Hiwin, and is sold by Voron-community-approved vendors as the expected alternative. For Voron builds, LDO rails are interchangeable with Hiwin and are the default recommendation when Hiwin is out of stock or unavailable.
Verdict Label: Licensed OEM supplier — consistently recommended alongside Hiwin by Voron-affiliated vendors
Cons:
Slightly softer brand recognition than Hiwin in wider motion control contexts — Hiwin remains the benchmark name
Availability depends on Voron-ecosystem vendors — not available through Misumi or standard industrial distributors
Name: LDO MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
LDO is a licensed manufacturer — not a quality clone, but a separate first-tier supplier approved by the Voron community
Sold by KB3D, Fabreeko, and Voron-official kit vendors as the expected rail choice
Consistently smooth with correct preload — community comparison builds show it matches Hiwin results

Description: Mellow is a Chinese linear motion manufacturer with an above-average reputation in the Voron and CoreXY community for quality clone rails. MGN9H from Mellow has a reasonable community track record, but buyers should budget time to clean and re-lube on arrival, and should expect to inspect and potentially reject an individual rail.
Verdict Label: Upper-tier quality clone — generally smooth, but you’re buying a quality distribution, not a guaranteed unit
Cons:
Still a quality distribution, not a specification — individual rails may have binding points or inconsistent preload
Requires cleaning and re-lubing on arrival regardless of seller claims
Cannot be returned easily from AliExpress if a defective rail arrives
Name: Mellow MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
Mellow has a positive reputation in the AliExpress ecosystem — fewer dead-on-arrival reports than generic alternatives
More affordable than Hiwin or LDO — meaningful cost savings on a 5-rail V2.4 build
Community has documented satisfactory results with Mellow rails on Voron builds
Sold pre-cleaned and lightly lubricated in most listings

Description: Anti-VFA belt conversion kit for CoreXY printers using GT1.5 (1.5mm pitch) belts instead of the standard GT2 (2mm pitch). The finer pitch halves the frequency interval between belt resonance harmonics, directly attacking variable frequency artifacts in print surface quality. Available in EPDM rubber (standard, from €69) and Powergrip rubber (premium, €139). Requires GT1.5-compatible pulleys and idlers — BRS sells matching printed PA12-CF hardware or you can use open-source files from their GitHub. BRS Engineering has official RatRig partnership.
Verdict Label: from €69 EUR | best anti-VFA belt upgrade available for RatRig/Voron
Cons:
Not a drop-in swap — requires compatible GT1.5 pulleys and idlers (printed or purchased)
Higher price point than GT2 replacement belts
Community still smaller than GT2 ecosystem
EU-based, lead times apply
Name: GT1.5 Anti-VFA Belt Conversion Kit
Pros:
GT1.5 pitch (1.5mm) vs standard GT2 (2mm) — half the resonance frequency interval
Directly reduces variable frequency artifacts (VFA/salmon skin) in prints
Available in EPDM (standard, from €69) and Powergrip rubber (premium, €139)
Open-source printed pulleys and idlers available from BRS GitHub
Official RatRig compatibility, community-proven on Voron builds

Description: Generic MGN9H rails from unspecified AliExpress sellers are a quality gamble. The lower price is offset by inconsistent preload, possible binding, and no path for returns on defective units. For a build where linear rail quality directly determines print quality, the savings do not justify the risk when Mellow (CONSIDER) and LDO/Hiwin (BUY) are available.
Verdict Label: Quality lottery — unknown manufacturer sourcing means no consistency guarantee
Cons:
No manufacturer accountability — quality varies not just by seller but by production batch
Binding, inconsistent preload, and corrosion have all been documented on unknown-brand AliExpress rails
Costs time to inspect, clean, and potentially return — savings often disappear in the hidden labor cost
Not worth the risk when Mellow or LDO are available at modest cost premium
Name: Generic MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
Cheapest way to source linear rails — meaningful savings if you happen to get a good batch
Some builders have had acceptable results and are willing to inspect and return bad units

Description: Hiwin MGN12H is used on the Voron 2.4 and Trident gantry Y rails and Z axes where span length and lateral load require the wider 12mm profile. The V2.4 uses MGN12H on both Y gantry rails and all four Z rails. Combined with titanium backers, MGN12H provides a rigid, repeatable foundation for the gantry.
Verdict Label: OEM 12mm rail — standard for V2.4 and Trident gantry and Z axis
Cons:
MGN12H is noticeably heavier than MGN9H — matters for X axis where carriage mass affects resonance frequency
More expensive per rail than MGN9 — a 4-rail V2.4 Z set is a significant BOM cost
Name: Hiwin MGN12H Linear Rail
Pros:
MGN12 is stiffer than MGN9 at equivalent length — correct choice for longer gantry spans and Z axes
H carriage preload handles lateral gantry forces during high-acceleration printing
Full Hiwin quality guarantees — no variance between rails in a matched set

Name: BFI - Beefy Front Idlers for Voron
V2.4 Ultimate Motion Kit with Gates Belts

Description: T8x8 400mm lead screws are used in the stock Voron 2.4 Z axis for 300mm and 350mm builds (4 screws). They work but are the most common first upgrade target. Belted Z is the official Voron Design upgrade path.
Verdict Label: Stock Z lead screw for 300mm and 350mm Voron V2.4 builds — functional but belted Z is the community upgrade
Cons:
Slower Z than belted Z — meaningful impact on multi-material and probing workflows
Ring resonance from lead screw whip is a documented problem at higher Z travel speeds
Requires Oldham couplers and periodic lubrication
Belted Z is the community-preferred upgrade
Name: T8 Lead Screw 8mm Lead 400mm
Pros:
Simple, well-understood Z motion — fully documented in V2.4 build guides
Low cost and easy to source in correct lengths
Works adequately for standard print speeds

Name: L3VER M2 Block with Tensioners Module

Description: The Voron 2.4 uses a belt-driven Z system as stock — each of the four corner Z motors drives a belt loop, and the printer has no lead screws. The result is fast Z travel, no screw-induced ringing, and low maintenance. This is the standard V2.4 Z setup, not an add-on upgrade.
Verdict Label: Official V2.4 Z upgrade — eliminates lead screw ringing and dramatically improves Z speed
Cons:
More complex installation than lead screws — belt tension must be set correctly on 4 independent Z belt paths
Requires Klipper firmware awareness — INPUT_SHAPER must account for changed Z resonance characteristics
Name: Voron 2.4 Belted Z
Pros:
Eliminates Z lead screw ringing — no more resonance artifacts from screw whip at higher Z speeds
Dramatically faster Z moves — meaningful improvement in multi-material and first-layer probing workflows
Open source, officially designed by Voron Design — full documentation, well-documented installation
Reuses most existing V2.4 motor hardware

Description: Gates LL-2GT 9mm belt is used in AWD CoreXY builds (RatRig V-Core 4, some VzBot configurations) where the wider belt handles the aggregate tension from 4 independent motor drives. The 9mm width is required when using 9mm pulleys and idlers; it is not a drop-in substitute for 6mm hardware.
Verdict Label: 9mm Gates belt for AWD builds — wider belt handles the higher forces of 4-motor drive
Cons:
9mm pulleys and idlers are required — cannot mix 6mm hardware with 9mm belt
Larger belt profile adds marginal mass to the gantry
Name: 2GT Belt 9mm
Pros:
Higher belt tension capacity than 6mm — appropriate for AWD drives where all 4 motor torques route through the belt simultaneously
Same Gates quality as 6mm — OEM specification, consistent stretch
Required for RatRig V-Core 4 AWD configuration — 6mm belt is undersized for 4-motor AWD tension

Description: Genuine GATES LL-1.5GT timing belt and pulley kit with CNC-machined aluminium drive and idler pulleys (27T/21T, 5mm bore) for 6/9/10/12mm belts; 1.5mm tooth pitch gives higher positioning precision and lower backlash than GT2.
Verdict Label: Genuine Gates GT1.5 belt and pulley kit — the best-verified value in the table
Cons:
Pulleys are Mellow’s own, not Gates — only the belts are genuine Gates
Kit spans four belt widths, so you must pick the right variant
GT1.5 is a niche standard — fewer guides and less community usage than GT2
Name: GATES-LL-1.5GT Belt Kit (6/9/10/12mm)
Pros:
Genuine GATES LL-1.5GT belts, not clones
CNC-machined aluminium drive and idler pulleys (27T/21T, 5mm bore)
1.5mm tooth pitch gives higher positioning precision and lower backlash than GT2
One kit covers 6/9/10/12mm belts
2.50 in stock at 3D Mellow

Description: F695 2RS flanged bearings are used at all smooth idler positions in Voron CoreXY belt paths — outer reversals where the belt’s flat back contacts the bearing. 5mm bore fits the M5 idler post and the flange retains belt laterally. Voron BOM specifies F695 2RS; note that quality varies significantly by source.
Verdict Label: Standard smooth idler for all Voron CoreXY belt path outer reversals
Cons:
Quality varies significantly by source — random AliExpress F695 may have gritty feel and short lifespan
Should be sourced from known vendors (Misumi, KB3D, Fabreeko) or confirmed reputable bearing suppliers
Name: F695 2RS Smooth Idler Bearing
Pros:
F695 2RS is the correct bearing spec — 5mm bore, 13mm OD, flanged
Flange retains the belt’s lateral position without a separate washer
Standard industrial bearing spec — available from reputable vendors at low cost

Name: V-Core 3/4 Z0 Preloaded HIWIN Rails Kit
V-Core 3/4 Z1 Preloaded HIWIN Rails Kit

Description: Ballscrew-based Z axis upgrade for RatRig V-Core 4.0 (version 4.0b). Replaces the stock leadscrew Z system with precision ballscrews — eliminating leadscrew wobble artifacts in the Z direction and improving positional repeatability. Available as hardware-only kit (€149, for builders with a printer) or full kit with PA12-CF printed parts (€262). Open-source printed part files on BRS GitHub. BRS Engineering has official RatRig partnership agreement.
Verdict Label: from €149 | significant improvement, non-trivial install
Cons:
Non-trivial installation — V-Core 4 Z frame disassembly required
Full kit €262 is a significant investment
Small install base compared to stock Z — less community troubleshooting documentation
EU-based, one-man shop — lead times apply
Name: Z-Upgrade 4.0b Ballscrew System
Pros:
Ballscrew Z axis — eliminates leadscrew backlash and wobble artifacts
Significant improvement in Z-axis positional accuracy and repeatability
Available hardware-only (€149) or full kit with PA12-CF printed parts (€262)
Official RatRig partnership — confirmed V-Core 4 compatibility
Open-source printed parts on BRS GitHub

Description: LDO MGN12H is the Voron-community-approved 12mm rail for V2.4 and Trident gantry and Z axes. It performs identically to Hiwin MGN12H at the same price point and is sold by the same Voron-affiliated vendors. Either LDO or Hiwin is the correct answer for a V2.4 MGN12H spec.
Verdict Label: Licensed OEM-quality 12mm rail — recommended for V2.4/Trident gantry and Z axis
Cons: Same weight and cost tradeoffs as Hiwin MGN12H — no meaningful difference in cons
Name: LDO MGN12H Linear Rail
Pros:
Same quality tier as Hiwin MGN12H from a licensed manufacturer — correct preload, consistent motion
Approved by Voron community vendor network — KB3D and Fabreeko ship LDO MGN12H in kit builds
Direct substitute for Hiwin MGN12H in all V2.4 and Trident configurations

Description: Oldham couplers are required at the motor-to-lead-screw junction on all Voron lead screw Z axes. They allow lateral float to accommodate shaft misalignment while transmitting rotation. Rigid shaft couplers are not a substitute — they will bind and cause Z banding.
Verdict Label: Essential companion to lead screw Z — eliminates Z binding from shaft misalignment
Cons:
Center disc wears over time and requires periodic inspection
Irrelevant if switching to belted Z
Name: Oldham Coupler
Pros:
Allows lateral float between motor shaft and lead screw — corrects for inevitable misalignment in assembled frames
Without Oldham couplers, misalignment binds Z and causes Z banding artifacts
Cheap, reliable, and non-negotiable on lead screw Z builds

Description: Hiwin MGN9H is the reference standard for linear motion in prosumer CoreXY printers. The 9mm profile is used on XY axes where low mass matters (Voron 0.2 on all axes, V2.4 and Trident on the X carriage). H carriages have factory-set preload that is consistent and reliable. All clone rail quality is benchmarked against Hiwin performance.
Verdict Label: The OEM reference standard — tight tolerances, consistent preload, zero quality lottery
Cons:
Expensive relative to clone options — a full Voron 2.4 rail set is a meaningful cost
Lead times and availability vary — Misumi cut-to-length is more reliably stocked than Hiwin direct
Name: Hiwin MGN9H Linear Rail
Pros:
Factory-set preload is consistent across the carriage — no binding at any point on the rail
H carriage (high preload) provides rigidity without being over-constrained
Tight machining tolerances — Hiwin is the benchmark all clone rails are measured against
Satisfied community documentation goes back years — well-understood failure modes

Name: GTC-19X26 High Vibration Damping Rubber Coupling
